newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 2.15 pct on economic worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 2.15 pct on economic worries.

text.p: Thai stocks declined 2.15 percent by lunch on Tuesday as investors sold on concerns that this week's small rate cuts by three banks were too little to alleviate the country's slowing economy, brokers said.

They also sold bank issues mainly on worries that the earnings of the financial institutions could fall if more of them were to follow three major banks who cut lending rates by 25 basis points, effective Tuesday, brokers added.
The SET index declined 14.44 points to 658.04 at 0454 GMT.

"Investors holding bank stocks are a bit jittery that bank earnings would be lower if they cut their interest rates and this forced them to sell," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securities.
Three major banks including Thai Farmers Bank Plc, Siam Commercial Bank Plc and Krung Thai Bank Plc announced a 25 basis point cut in their minimum lending rates on Monday.
At 0515 GMT the index slipped further to 657.77, down 14.71 points, or 2.19 percent. Bangkok Bank was off 5.00 at 173 and Krung Thai Bank down 0.30 to 33 baht.- S.Chawla (662) 652-0642
